name: UPSC / Civil Services
description: Civil Services (Prelims) style questions: Indian polity, modern history, geography, economy and environment.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can President's Rule be imposed in a state?
questions.explanation: Article 356 provides for President's Rule on failure of constitutional machinery in a state. Article 352 is National Emergency, 360 is Financial Emergency.

questions.question: The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part III (Articles 12–35) contains the Fundamental Rights. Part IV has the Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: The President appoints the CJI under Article 124, acting on the recommendation of the outgoing CJI / collegium (established by the Second and Third Judges Cases).

questions.question: A Money Bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only on the recommendation of whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 117(1), a Money Bill requires the President's recommendation before introduction in the Lok Sabha, and it cannot originate in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) is popularly known as what?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment, passed during the Emergency, altered the Preamble and dozens of provisions — hence the 'Mini Constitution' tag.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part IV (Articles 36–51) lists the DPSPs, borrowed largely from the Irish Constitution. Part IVA has the Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: What is the term of a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha members serve 6-year terms, with one-third retiring every two years — the House is a permanent body.

questions.question: A National Emergency is proclaimed under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 352 deals with National Emergency (war, external aggression, armed rebellion). It has been proclaimed three times: 1962, 1971 and 1975.

questions.question: Who has the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha under Article 85, on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved.

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) is related to which subject?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment constitutionalised Panchayati Raj (three-tier rural local government). The 74th Amendment covers urban Municipalities.

questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757) — Robert Clive's victory over Siraj-ud-Daulah — laid the foundation of British rule in India. Buxar followed in 1764.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy, became the first Governor-General of independent India (Aug 1947 – June 1948). C. Rajagopalachari was the first Indian to hold the post.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March, marking the start of the Civil Disobedience Movement, took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Salt March from Sabarmati to Dandi (12 March – 6 April 1930) launched the Civil Disobedience Movement against the salt tax.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which year?
questions.explanation: On 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi), troops under General Dyer fired on an unarmed gathering at Amritsar — a turning point of the freedom struggle.

questions.question: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (now Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee set up on 29 August 1947.

questions.question: The Chauri Chaura incident (1922) led Mahatma Gandhi to withdraw which movement?
questions.explanation: After policemen were killed by a mob at Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922), Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement, insisting on non-violence.

questions.question: The Simla Agreement of 1972 was signed between India and which country?
questions.explanation: Signed by Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto after the 1971 war, the Simla Agreement committed both nations to resolving disputes bilaterally.

questions.question: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble during the Emergency.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.explanation: It passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.question: Which Indian mountain range is geologically older — the Himalayas or the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats (block mountains, formed during Gondwana breakup) are far older than the young fold mountains of the Himalayas.

questions.question: Which river is historically known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal'?
questions.explanation: The Damodar's devastating floods earned it the name 'Sorrow of Bengal'; the DVC project later tamed it. The Kosi is the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

questions.question: The southwest monsoon normally arrives over the Kerala coast around which time?
questions.explanation: The monsoon 'onset' over Kerala is around 1 June (normal date), progressing northward to cover the country by mid-July.

questions.question: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) established?
questions.explanation: The RBI began operations on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act 1934 (Hilton Young Commission's recommendation). It was nationalised in 1949.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) came into force across India on which date?
questions.explanation: GST — 'One Nation, One Tax' — was launched at midnight on 1 July 2017, via the 101st Constitutional Amendment.

questions.question: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is related to the conservation of what?
questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention is an international treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands; India has 80+ Ramsar sites.

questions.question: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 from Jim Corbett National Park; India hosts ~70% of the world's wild tigers.

questions.question: India's first nuclear test, code-named 'Smiling Buddha', was conducted in which year?
questions.explanation: 'Smiling Buddha' was a peaceful nuclear explosion at Pokhran on 18 May 1974. Pokhran-II followed in 1998.

questions.question: Which constitutional body conducts the Civil Services Examination (IAS/IPS)?
questions.explanation: The Union Public Service Commission (Articles 315–323) conducts the CSE for the IAS, IPS, IFS and other All-India Services.

questions.question: The National Emergency declared on 25 June 1975 was proclaimed during the prime ministership of whom?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi's government declared the 21-month Emergency citing 'internal disturbance' — the only Emergency on that ground.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Article 14 guarantees equality before law, 19 the freedoms, and 21 protection of life and personal liberty.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles were modelled on the Irish Constitution, which had itself drawn on Spanish precedent. Fundamental Rights came from the US, federal structure with a strong centre from Canada, and the Concurrent List from Australia.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age in India from 21 to 18 years?
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment of 1988 reduced the voting age to 18. The 42nd is the wide-ranging 1976 amendment, the 44th reversed much of it, and the 73rd created panchayati raj.

questions.question: In which case did the Supreme Court of India first articulate the basic structure doctrine?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament cannot alter the Constitution's basic structure. Golaknath had earlier barred amendment of Fundamental Rights outright, while Minerva Mills later reinforced the doctrine.

questions.question: Who is the constitutional head of the Union Public Service Commission's appointment process?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Article 316 empowers the President to appoint the Chairman and members of the UPSC. The Prime Minister advises but does not appoint, and the judiciary has no role in it.

questions.question: How many schedules does the Constitution of India contain?
questions.explanation: The Constitution has twelve schedules; it began with eight, and the Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh and Twelfth were added by later amendments.

questions.question: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with which subject?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985, contains the anti-defection law. Languages are in the Eighth Schedule, panchayats in the Eleventh, and protected land reform laws in the Ninth.

questions.question: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court of India to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Article 32 gives the Supreme Court writ jurisdiction for Fundamental Rights and is itself a Fundamental Right. Article 226 gives High Courts wider writ powers, 136 covers special leave to appeal, and 143 the President's reference.

questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Article 60 provides that the Chief Justice of India, or in their absence the senior-most Supreme Court judge, administers the President's oath.

questions.question: Which house of the Indian Parliament cannot be dissolved?
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body with one-third of its members retiring every two years. The Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President before its five-year term ends.

questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Gandhi launched Quit India in August 1942 with the call to 'do or die'. 1930 saw the Civil Disobedience Movement, 1920 Non-Cooperation, and 1945 the Simla Conference.

questions.question: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
questions.explanation: A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, was the founder and first general secretary. W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session, and Naoroji was president three times later.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 was fought between the British East India Company and which ruler?
questions.explanation: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, after Mir Jafar defected and was installed in his place. Tipu Sultan and Hyder Ali fought the later Anglo-Mysore Wars.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal at Agra as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal. Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri, and Aurangzeb, his son, later deposed him.

questions.question: The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy associated with which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie used the Doctrine of Lapse to annex states without a natural heir, including Satara and Jhansi. Curzon partitioned Bengal, Ripon is known for local self-government, and Cornwallis for the Permanent Settlement.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which city?
questions.explanation: Troops under General Dyer fired on an unarmed gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar in April 1919, killing hundreds.

questions.question: The Ryotwari system of land revenue was introduced primarily in which region of British India?
questions.explanation: The Ryotwari system, settling revenue directly with individual cultivators, was applied mainly in the Madras and Bombay presidencies. Bengal and Bihar had the Permanent Settlement with zamindars.

questions.question: Which session of the Indian National Congress adopted the resolution for Purna Swaraj?
questions.explanation: The Lahore session of December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted Purna Swaraj, and independence was declared on 26 January 1930. The Karachi session of 1931 adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Ashoka's inscriptions were first successfully deciphered by which scholar?
questions.explanation: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837, making Ashoka's edicts readable. Cunningham founded the Archaeological Survey, and Marshall later directed the Indus Valley excavations.

questions.question: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari, at roughly 1,465 km, is the longest river lying wholly within India. The Ganga is longer overall but continues into Bangladesh.

questions.question: Which mountain pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
questions.explanation: Zoji La on the Srinagar–Leh highway is the key link to Ladakh. Nathu La is in Sikkim, Rohtang in Himachal Pradesh, and Shipki La on the Sutlej route to Tibet.

questions.question: Which soil type covers the largest area of the Deccan plateau and is best suited to cotton?
questions.explanation: Black or regur soil, formed from weathered basalt lava, retains moisture well and dominates the Deccan trap region where cotton is grown. Alluvial soil dominates the northern plains instead.

questions.question: The Palk Strait separates India from which country?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka, connecting the Bay of Bengal with the Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain peak located entirely within India?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi in Uttarakhand is the highest peak wholly inside India. Kanchenjunga is higher but sits on the border with Nepal.

questions.question: The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet at which range of hills?
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Hills form the junction of the Western and Eastern Ghats. The Anaimalai, Cardamom and Palani hills all lie within the Western Ghats system further south.

questions.question: Which body in India is responsible for setting the policy repo rate?
options: The Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: The Monetary Policy Committee, constituted under the RBI Act, sets the repo rate by majority vote. SEBI regulates securities markets and NITI Aayog is a policy think tank with no rate-setting role.

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax was introduced in India by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 101st Amendment of 2016 enabled GST and created the GST Council. The 99th created the struck-down NJAC, the 97th dealt with cooperative societies, and the 103rd with EWS reservation.

questions.question: In national income accounting, what does the term 'net factor income from abroad' distinguish?
questions.explanation: Gross National Product equals Gross Domestic Product plus net factor income from abroad. Depreciation is what separates gross from net measures, and a price deflator separates nominal from real.

questions.question: Which committee recommended the inflation-targeting framework adopted by the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: The Urjit Patel Committee of 2014 recommended a flexible inflation-targeting regime anchored to consumer price inflation. The Narasimham committees dealt with banking sector reform.

questions.question: Which organisation publishes India's Consumer Price Index?
questions.explanation: The National Statistical Office under MoSPI compiles and releases the CPI. The Ministry of Commerce publishes the Wholesale Price Index instead.

questions.question: What does the term 'fiscal deficit' measure in the Indian budget?
options: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
questions.explanation: The fiscal deficit is total expenditure less total receipts other than borrowings, so it measures how much the government must borrow. Revenue expenditure less revenue receipts is the revenue deficit.

questions.question: Project Tiger was launched in India in which year?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger began in 1973 with nine reserves. The Wildlife Protection Act came in 1972 and the Environment Protection Act in 1986.

questions.question: The Montreal Protocol concerns the phasing out of which class of substances?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 phases out ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs. Greenhouse gases fall under the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement, and persistent organic pollutants under the Stockholm Convention.

questions.question: Which Indian wetland was the first to be designated a Ramsar site along with Keoladeo National Park?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake in Odisha and Keoladeo in Rajasthan were India's first two Ramsar sites, both designated in 1981. Loktak, Wular and Sambhar were added in 1990.

questions.question: In the IUCN Red List, which category indicates the highest risk of extinction for a species still found in the wild?
questions.explanation: Critically Endangered is the highest risk category for wild species, above Endangered and Vulnerable. Extinct in the Wild and Extinct lie beyond it but mean the species no longer survives in nature.

questions.question: India's Mars Orbiter Mission was launched by which vehicle?
questions.explanation: PSLV-C25 launched the Mars Orbiter Mission in November 2013, and it entered Martian orbit the following September. The GSLV series is used for heavier geostationary payloads.

questions.question: Which gas makes up the largest proportion of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen accounts for about 78% of the atmosphere by volume, with oxygen close to 21% and argon under 1%.

questions.question: The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre is located in which city?
questions.explanation: BARC's main campus is at Trombay in Mumbai. Kalpakkam hosts the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research, and Indore the Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology.

questions.question: Which Indian scientist received the Nobel Prize in Physics for work on the scattering of light?
questions.explanation: C. V. Raman won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for the Raman effect. Chandrasekhar won in 1983 for stellar structure, while Bose and Bhabha never received the prize.

questions.question: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal in 1793 was introduced by which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement, fixing land revenue with zamindars in perpetuity. Warren Hastings preceded him and Wellesley is associated with the subsidiary alliance system.

questions.question: The Subsidiary Alliance system in India was devised by which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley used the subsidiary alliance to bring Indian states under British control by stationing troops at their expense. Dalhousie later used the doctrine of lapse for outright annexation.

questions.question: Which Indus Valley site is known for its dockyard, indicating maritime trade?
questions.explanation: Lothal in Gujarat has a large brick basin identified as a dockyard. Kalibangan is known for ploughed fields and Dholavira for its water management and signboard.

questions.question: Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the conquest of which kingdom?
questions.explanation: The bloodshed of the Kalinga war led Ashoka to Buddhism, as recorded in his thirteenth rock edict. Magadha was already the Mauryan heartland.

questions.question: The Gupta ruler who assumed the title 'Vikramaditya' and is credited with defeating the Shakas was
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II took the title Vikramaditya after defeating the Western Shakas. Samudragupta is known from the Allahabad pillar inscription and Skandagupta for repelling the Hunas.

questions.question: Who founded the Arya Samaj in 1875?
questions.explanation: Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj with the call to return to the Vedas. Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj decades earlier, and Vivekananda the Ramakrishna Mission later.

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in which year?
questions.explanation: Non-Cooperation began in 1920 and was withdrawn after Chauri Chaura in 1922. Civil Disobedience followed in 1930 and Quit India in 1942.

questions.question: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed which arrangement for India?
options: A federal union with grouping of provinces
Continued direct British rule for ten years
A unitary state with no provincial autonomy
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission proposed a loose federal union with provinces grouped into sections, rejecting a separate Pakistan. Partition came instead through the Mountbatten Plan of 1947.

questions.question: Who wrote the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', setting out the drain of wealth theory?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji set out the drain of wealth theory in this work. R. C. Dutt wrote the Economic History of India, developing related arguments.

questions.question: The Indian National Army was reorganised and led from 1943 by
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose took command of the INA in 1943 after Rash Behari Bose handed it over. Mohan Singh had raised the first INA in 1942, and Bhagat Singh had been executed in 1931.

questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was enacted during the viceroyalty of
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton passed the Vernacular Press Act to curb Indian-language newspapers. His successor Lord Ripon repealed it in 1882.

questions.question: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 are chiefly remembered for introducing
questions.explanation: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims. Dyarchy came with the 1919 reforms and provincial autonomy with the Government of India Act of 1935.

questions.question: Which strait separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands?
questions.explanation: The Ten Degree Channel lies between the Andaman and Nicobar groups. The Nine Degree Channel separates Lakshadweep islands, and Duncan Passage lies within the Andamans.

questions.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline of any Indian state, owing to its deeply indented shore and the gulfs of Kachchh and Khambhat.

questions.question: The Narmada and Tapi rivers are unusual among peninsular rivers because they
options: Flow westward into the Arabian Sea through rift valleys
Form large deltas on the east coast
questions.explanation: The Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys and form estuaries rather than deltas, unlike most peninsular rivers which flow east into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India by area?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is India's largest freshwater lake. Chilika and Vembanad are brackish lagoons and Sambhar is a salt lake.

questions.question: The Deccan Plateau is bounded on the north by which range?
questions.explanation: The Satpura range marks the northern edge of the Deccan Plateau. The Aravallis lie further north-west in Rajasthan and the Shivaliks form the Himalayan foothills.

questions.question: Which local wind brings destructive summer storms to eastern India, known as Kalbaisakhi?
questions.explanation: Norwesters, called Kalbaisakhi in Bengal, are violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms. The Loo is a hot dry wind of the northern plains and mango showers are pre-monsoon rain in the south.

questions.question: The Indian Standard Time meridian passes through which longitude?
questions.explanation: IST is based on the 82°30′ E meridian passing near Mirzapur, which is five and a half hours ahead of Greenwich.

questions.question: Which Indian state shares the longest border with Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: West Bengal has the longest stretch of the India-Bangladesh border. Tripura, Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram share shorter sections.

questions.question: Laterite soil in India is formed chiefly as a result of
options: Intense leaching in high rainfall and high temperature
questions.explanation: Laterite forms where heavy rain and heat leach away silica, leaving iron and aluminium oxides. Alluvium is river-deposited and black soil derives from basalt.

questions.question: The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, lies in the delta of which river system?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans occupy the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta across India and Bangladesh. The Narmada and Tapi form estuaries rather than deltas.

questions.question: Which pass connects India with China in Sikkim and was reopened for border trade in 2006?
questions.explanation: Nathu La in Sikkim reopened for trade in 2006 after being closed since the 1962 war. Zoji La and Rohtang are internal passes in the western Himalaya.

questions.question: El Nino, which can weaken the Indian monsoon, refers to the warming of which ocean region?
options: The central and eastern equatorial Pacific
questions.explanation: El Nino is the warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, which shifts atmospheric circulation and is often associated with deficient Indian monsoon rainfall.

questions.question: The cash reserve ratio in India refers to the share of deposits banks must hold
options: As reserves with the Reserve Bank of India
As cash in their own vaults only
questions.explanation: CRR is the proportion of net demand and time liabilities kept as reserves with the RBI. The statutory liquidity ratio is the separate requirement to hold liquid assets such as government securities.

questions.question: Which rate is the interest at which the Reserve Bank of India lends to commercial banks against securities?
questions.explanation: The repo rate is charged when the RBI lends short term against securities. The reverse repo is the rate at which it absorbs funds from banks instead.

questions.question: The Human Development Index published by UNDP combines income with which two other dimensions?
questions.explanation: HDI combines life expectancy for health, schooling measures for education, and gross national income per capita. Inequality is treated separately in the inequality-adjusted HDI.

questions.question: In India, which sector is classified as the tertiary sector?
questions.explanation: The tertiary sector covers services such as trade, transport, banking and IT. Agriculture is primary, while manufacturing and mining fall under primary and secondary activity.

questions.question: Demand-pull inflation arises primarily from
options: A rise in input costs such as wages and fuel
A fall in the money supply
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation occurs when demand outstrips the economy's capacity to supply. Rising input costs instead produce cost-push inflation.

questions.question: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in India in which year?
questions.explanation: The FRBM Act of 2003 set targets for reducing fiscal and revenue deficits. Liberalisation began in 1991 and the GST regime in 2017.

questions.question: Disguised unemployment is most characteristic of which sector in India?
questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment means more people work on a holding than are needed, so removing some would not reduce output. This is typical of Indian agriculture.

questions.question: The Gini coefficient is a measure of
questions.explanation: The Gini coefficient runs from zero for perfect equality to one for perfect inequality. It is derived from the Lorenz curve and says nothing about growth or inflation.

questions.question: Which institution regulates the insurance sector in India?
questions.explanation: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India regulates insurers. SEBI regulates securities markets, the RBI banks, and PFRDA pensions.

questions.question: Bank nationalisation in India first took place on a large scale in which year?
questions.explanation: Fourteen major commercial banks were nationalised in 1969, with six more in 1980. The State Bank of India had been created earlier in 1955.

questions.question: The Convention on Biological Diversity was opened for signature at which summit?
questions.explanation: The CBD was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992, alongside the UNFCCC. Stockholm 1972 produced the declaration that led to UNEP.

questions.question: Which gas is chiefly responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: Chlorine released from CFCs destroys ozone catalytically in the stratosphere. Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases affecting warming rather than ozone.

questions.question: A biosphere reserve differs from a national park chiefly in that it
options: Includes a core, buffer and transition zone allowing regulated human activity
Is designated only for a single species
Is managed solely by local panchayats
questions.explanation: Biosphere reserves are zoned into core, buffer and transition areas, permitting sustainable use outside the core. National parks apply stricter uniform protection.

questions.question: Which Indian institution releases the State of Forest Report?
questions.explanation: The Forest Survey of India, based at Dehradun, assesses forest cover and publishes the biennial State of Forest Report.

questions.question: The Paris Agreement adopted in 2015 aims to limit global temperature rise this century to
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement seeks to hold warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.

questions.question: Eutrophication of a water body is caused primarily by
options: Excess nutrients such as nitrates and phosphates
questions.explanation: Nutrient enrichment from fertiliser and sewage triggers algal blooms, which deplete dissolved oxygen when they decay and kill aquatic life.

questions.question: The Great Indian Bustard, a critically endangered bird, is the state bird of which state?
questions.explanation: The Great Indian Bustard is Rajasthan's state bird, with the Desert National Park a key habitat. Small populations survive in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

questions.question: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission achieved a soft landing near which region of the Moon?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023, making India the first country to do so.

questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor for red cell transfusion?
questions.explanation: O negative red cells carry neither A, B nor Rh D antigens, so they can be given to almost any recipient. AB positive is the universal recipient instead.

questions.question: The pH value of a neutral solution at 25°C is
questions.explanation: A neutral solution has equal hydrogen and hydroxide ion concentrations, giving pH 7 at 25°C. Values below 7 are acidic and above 7 alkaline.

questions.question: Which vitamin is synthesised in human skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet B light converts a cholesterol derivative in skin into vitamin D. Vitamin C and K come from diet, and vitamin A from carotenoids and animal sources.

questions.question: ISRO's launch site at Sriharikota is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota is in Andhra Pradesh. Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala hosts VSSC, which develops launch vehicles.

questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by which authority?
questions.explanation: Article 148 provides that the President appoints the CAG, who can be removed only in the manner prescribed for a Supreme Court judge. Parliament examines the CAG's reports but does not appoint the office.

questions.question: Which writ is issued to a public official to compel performance of a public duty?
questions.explanation: Mandamus commands an authority to perform a duty it has failed to discharge. Habeas corpus produces a detained person, certiorari quashes a lower order, and quo warranto challenges a person's title to an office.

questions.question: The Finance Commission of India is constituted under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission every five years to recommend distribution of taxes between the Union and the states. Article 324 covers the Election Commission and 315 the public service commissions.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.explanation: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. The Sarkaria Commission dealt with centre-state relations and Balwant Rai Mehta with panchayati raj.

questions.question: Under the Constitution, residuary powers of legislation belong to
questions.explanation: Article 248 vests residuary powers, over matters in none of the three lists, in Parliament. This follows the Canadian model of a strong centre rather than the American one.

questions.question: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The President nominates twelve members distinguished in literature, science, art and social service. The nomination of two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha was discontinued in 2020.

questions.question: The Election Commission of India was made a multi-member body permanently in which year?
questions.explanation: The Commission became permanently multi-member in 1993 with two Election Commissioners alongside the Chief Election Commissioner. A brief multi-member phase in 1989 had been reversed.

questions.question: A Constitutional Amendment Bill affecting the federal structure requires ratification by
options: At least half the state legislatures
questions.explanation: Amendments touching federal provisions need a special majority in Parliament plus ratification by the legislatures of at least half the states. Ordinary amendments need only the special majority.

questions.question: Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting. The Vice-President chairs the Rajya Sabha but does not preside over joint sittings.

questions.question: The concept of 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 was expanded to include due process in which case?
options: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
A. K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
questions.explanation: Maneka Gandhi (1978) held that any procedure must be fair, just and reasonable, effectively importing due process. A. K. Gopalan had earlier read Article 21 narrowly.

questions.question: The National Human Rights Commission of India was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The NHRC was set up in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act. It is a statutory body rather than a constitutional one.

questions.question: Which schedule of the Constitution lists the official languages of India?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule lists the scheduled languages. The Seventh contains the legislative lists, the Ninth protected laws, and the Sixth tribal area administration in the north-east.

questions.question: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was opposed because it allowed
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act permitted detention without trial and trial without jury, prompting nationwide protest and the events at Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.question: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced which system in the provinces?
options: Separate electorates for the first time
questions.explanation: The 1935 Act replaced provincial dyarchy with provincial autonomy and introduced dyarchy at the centre instead. Separate electorates dated from 1909.

questions.question: Who led the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928?
questions.explanation: Vallabhbhai Patel led the Bardoli Satyagraha against a revenue increase, earning the title Sardar. Rajendra Prasad had earlier worked with Gandhi at Champaran.

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The first session met at Bombay in December 1885 under W. C. Bonnerjee. It had been planned for Poona but was moved because of a cholera outbreak.

questions.question: The Partition of Bengal announced in 1905 was carried out by
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, triggering the Swadeshi movement. The partition was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge.

questions.question: Which movement did Mahatma Gandhi launch in Champaran in 1917?
questions.explanation: Champaran was Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, on behalf of indigo cultivators forced into the tinkathia system. Non-Cooperation followed in 1920.

questions.question: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was fought between the Marathas and
questions.explanation: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas at Panipat in 1761. The first battle in 1526 was Babur against Ibrahim Lodi, and the second in 1556 involved Akbar's forces.

questions.question: The Sarnath Lion Capital, adopted as India's State Emblem, was erected by which ruler?
questions.explanation: The Lion Capital was erected by Ashoka at Sarnath, where the Buddha gave his first sermon. Its wheel appears on the national flag.

questions.question: Which crop is a kharif crop in India?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the southwest monsoon and harvested in autumn, rice being the principal one. Wheat, mustard and barley are rabi crops sown in winter.

questions.question: The Palghat Gap, an important break in the Western Ghats, lies between which two states?
questions.explanation: The Palghat Gap connects Kerala with Tamil Nadu and carries major road and rail routes. It also influences rainfall and species distribution across the Ghats.

questions.question: Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: Anamudi in Kerala is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India. Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris and Mullayanagiri in Karnataka.

questions.question: The Thar Desert lies mainly in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Thar or Great Indian Desert lies mostly in western Rajasthan, extending into parts of Gujarat, Haryana and Punjab and across into Pakistan.

questions.question: The Indian monsoon retreats from the subcontinent in which season, bringing rain to Tamil Nadu?
options: The northeast monsoon in October to December
questions.explanation: The retreating or northeast monsoon brings most of Tamil Nadu's rainfall between October and December, when the rest of India is drying out.

questions.question: The New Economic Policy of liberalisation in India was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: The 1991 reforms, prompted by a balance of payments crisis, liberalised industrial licensing, trade and foreign investment.

questions.question: Priority sector lending norms in India require banks to lend to sectors including
questions.explanation: Priority sector lending directs credit to agriculture, micro and small enterprises, education, housing and weaker sections, which might otherwise be underserved.

questions.question: A country's balance of payments current account records
options: Trade in goods and services, income and transfers
Changes in foreign exchange reserves alone
questions.explanation: The current account covers merchandise trade, services, primary income and current transfers. Investment flows are recorded in the capital and financial accounts.

questions.question: The Green Revolution in India was associated most closely with which crops?
questions.explanation: High-yielding varieties of wheat and later rice drove the Green Revolution from the 1960s, concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Which Indian Act provides the legal framework for protecting wild animals and plants?
questions.explanation: The Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 lists protected species in its schedules and provides for national parks and sanctuaries. The 1986 Act is the broader umbrella environmental law.

questions.question: How many biodiversity hotspots recognised globally lie wholly or partly within India?
questions.explanation: Four hotspots touch India: the Himalaya, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland covering the Nicobar Islands.

questions.question: The National Green Tribunal was established in India in which year?
questions.explanation: The NGT was set up in 2010 to hear environmental cases speedily. The Environment Protection Act dates from 1986 and the Biological Diversity Act from 2002.

questions.question: Which part of the human brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates movement and maintains balance. The cerebrum handles higher thought, the medulla controls breathing and heartbeat, and the hypothalamus regulates hormones.

questions.question: Which ISRO launch vehicle is nicknamed the 'Bahubali' for its heavy-lift capability?
questions.explanation: GSLV Mk III, later designated LVM3, is India's heaviest launcher and carried Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3. The PSLV is a workhorse for lighter payloads.

questions.question: The greenhouse effect on Earth is caused by atmospheric gases absorbing which radiation?
questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases are largely transparent to incoming shortwave sunlight but absorb the longwave infrared the surface re-emits, trapping heat in the lower atmosphere.
